newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Nuveen expanding beyond munis.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Nuveen expanding beyond munis.

text.p: John Nuveen Co.'s planned acquisition of Rittenhouse Financial Services is part of an ongoing expansion beyond the company's traditional muni market focus, Nuveen Chairman Timothy Schwertfeger said.

"Financial advisers and investors have come to think of Nuveen more broadly than tax-free... and there was an openness and willingness to accept a broader array of product," Schwertfeger said in a telephone interview. "The core of our strategy is to find ways to expand the investment services that we offer."

Nuveen announced Tuesday it had agreed to acquire Rittenhouse, which focuses mainly on equity investments, in a cash purchase of $145 million expected to close by the end of September. Rittenhouse manages about $9 billion in assets, compared to Nuveen's roughly $50 billion under management.

"The Rittenhouse investment philosophy and investment process is focused upon financially strong companies who are number one in their industry and have a proven track record of consistent growth in earnings and dividends," Schwertfeger said.
That investment style appeals to clients of Nuveen, many of whom are at or near retirement age and "have a strong orientation toward preservation of capital," Schwertfeger said.
Nuveen began to expand beyond the tax-exempt market in late 1996, when it launched its first equity and balanced mutual funds. The three funds now have assets totaling more than $800 million.

Schwertfeger contrasted the Rittenhouse acquisition to Nuveen's purchase of Flagship Resources in January. The Flagship deal was aimed more at strengthening Nuveen's existing municipal base rather than its planned expansion into other areas, he said.

The Nuveen chairman said it was company policy not to discuss other potential acquisitions, but added that "we are always seeking to complement Nuveen's existing expertise by either building from within the firm or partnering with organizations that can better serve our investors and their advisers."
Under the terms of the Rittenhouse acquisition, there will be no management changes and the company will continue to operate from its base in Radnor, Pa.
"They've got a great group of people who are doing a tremendous job and we want to support them as much as we can," Schwertfeger said.
CoreStates Financial Corp announced plans in 1994 to acquire Rittenhouse for $55 million, but the deal was called off before the transaction was completed.

In conjunction with the Rittenhouse announcement Tuesday, Nuveen also announced second quarter earnings per share of $0.51, an 11 percent increase from the $0.46 per share in the same period last year.
Second quarter net income was $17.7 million, compared with $17.2 million in 1996.
